title: Understand data-model implications while designing
statement: As an Architect defining a new design, I can see its ERD implications in the technical overview alongside the existing application data model so I can reason about how the proposed work changes the application's data.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The technical overview provides an application-wide ERD entry point showing existing data entities and the entities and relationships implicated by the selected design.
The model can describe both logical payloads and persisted records, including a JSON PDF-generation job in a queue and the PDF report record produced from it, with their storage resources identified.

The ERD visually distinguishes the meaning of data relationships, including logical production/transformation and persisted associations, and exposes declared cardinality without inventing unknown relationships.
A proposed entity or relationship change can be followed to the design and feature context that introduces it without overwriting the baseline model.

The ERD is an authored, human-consumable architectural diagram whose selected entities, composition, and relationships convey the overall shape of the application rather than an automatically generated schema dump.

Authors can show only architecturally meaningful fields and keys; the ERD does not require an exhaustive mirror of database columns or payload properties, and omitted field detail does not imply missing implementation.
